items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Cozy Cole) is not present in the transcript; the mention of Cannonball Adderly is made by the Interviewer and another person (Ivan) in a conversation about Eddie Lockjaw Davis. Cozy Cole is merely addressed by name ('Oh, Cozy') but does not speak or provide personal insight.

ctx.x: Yeah, I'm told he's playing mostly tenor now.

Yeah, tenor. And Ivan said to me, he says, Oh, Cozy, Eddie's talking about that saxophone's a faggot's instrument. So Ivan said to him, he said, was Cannonball Adderly a faggot, or was Charlie Parker a faggot, and Eddie said 'No, well they were exceptions.' So he's playing tenor now. But he's a great musician.
He was a great lead alto player.

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Cannonball Adderley in a list of musicians associated with the Metropole, but the interviewee (Cozy Cole) does not respond to confirm any personal interaction or relationship.

ctx.x: Hamp with a big band, that's right, Gene Krupa, Diz, Adderley--Cannonball, him and Nat Adderley, and so you remember some awful nice times working in there, in the Metropole. Well the one who really built that Metropole was Henry Red Allen. He had a number he used to do, 'Kiss the Baby.' People used to come from all over the world if they had a new date, to come in and holler up at Red, 'play 'Kiss the Baby.' And they'd play 'Kiss the Baby.'
Here's someone we really hadn't touched on.
